proposal.utterance: Classify 'Abusus' (the right of abuse, in Roman-law property theory) in BFO terms.

entities.label: Abusus
entities.rationale: Abusus is the right (ius) to consume, destroy, or alienate a thing — one of the three classic sticks in Roman dominium alongside usus and fructus. As a kind of legal right, it is a role borne by a legal person with respect to a corporeal thing: it is externally grounded in the legal system that recognises ownership, it inheres in its bearer (the dominus), and it is realised in acts of alienation, destruction, or consumption. It therefore types as a Role (BFO_0000023) and is naturally a subclass of the existing working:LegalRight class (itself typed as BFO_0000023). It is a class (a kind of right), not an individual instance.

entities.label: ActOfAlienation
entities.rationale: Abusus is realised in processes of alienation, destruction, or consumption of the thing owned. ActOfAlienation (a Process) represents the class of such realising occurrents. It is the canonical realisation vehicle for the Abusus role, needed to state the BFO_0000054 (realized in) relation.

relations.rationale: Abusus is a specific kind of LegalRight (a right pertaining to ownership over a corporeal thing), inheriting its Role typing from that parent.

The Abusus role is realised in processes of alienation, consumption, or destruction — represented by ActOfAlienation. BFO_0000054 (realized in) links a realizable entity to the process type in which it is exercised.

open_questions: Should 'Abusus' be modelled as an individual instance (the single Roman-law concept of abusus) rather than a class (a kind of right that multiple owners can instantiate)? The current proposal treats it as a class, which allows asserting that specific owners bear instances of Abusus.
Should we also model 'Usus' (right of use) and 'Fructus' (right of fruits) as sibling subclasses of LegalRight now, to complete the Roman dominium triad and make the partition explicit?

The bearer of Abusus is a legal person (dominus) with respect to a corporeal thing (res). Should we add a 'Dominium' class (or use an existing material-entity class) and explicitly assert that Abusus inheres in (RO_0000052) a Dominus role-bearer?
ActOfAlienation is introduced as the paradigm realisation process. Should we also include ActOfDestruction and ActOfConsumption as sub-processes, or collapse them into one class?
proposal.rationale_summary: Abusus, the Roman-law right to alienate or destroy a thing, is a species of legal right and is therefore typed as a Role (BFO_0000023): it is an externally grounded, socially recognised power that inheres in the owner (dominus) with respect to a corporeal object. It belongs under the existing working:LegalRight class, which is already typed as BFO_0000023. Because BFO roles are realisable entities, they must be linked via BFO_0000054 (realized in) to the processes in which they are exercised; a new class ActOfAlienation (BFO_0000015 Process) is introduced as the canonical realisation vehicle. Both entities are proposed as classes (kinds), not individuals, because the ontology is intended to support assertions about many particular owners bearing instances of Abusus. Open questions concern whether to also model the companion rights Usus and Fructus, how to represent the bearer (dominus) and the object (res) of the right, and whether the realisation processes need finer granularity.
